numerics.observation_reason: R0033 reports the original T+120 s checkpoint and extends observation to T+1500 s to distinguish slow recovery from persistent residual. Observation is not a controller parameter; all acceptance tolerances are unchanged.

Retired mathematical floor of zero, kept as the contrast to the wing-borne floor now used as the nominal. A zero floor lets the aircraft hover mid-corridor, which is a flight-mode change rather than a slow-down, so it is not an operational option.

provenance.vehicle_bounds: synthetic mechanism assumptions; zero floor is legacy mathematical case; 30 m/s floor and 80 m/s cap are sourced separately below, not calibrated
provenance.controller: Unchanged gains; established pairs use signed gap/relative-speed feedback without the nominal-cruise veto. Non-established distant leaders do not trigger pursuit. This is the straight-route pair integration, not full-corridor relationship management.
provenance.leader_observation: perfect continuous current state including acceleration; no sensing latency
provenance.jerk: reference trajectory only; feedback/fallback jerk not constrained
provenance.scope: R0033: six established-pair transitions plus six variants; no continuous geographic fallback traversal, multi-aircraft or capacity result.
provenance.speed_min_mps: 1.2 x Vstall for a low-wing-loading eVTOL: the preferred design band gives Vstall <= 50 kt = 25.7 m/s, so 1.2 Vstall = 30.9 m/s. Below this the aircraft is no longer wing-borne, which is a flight-mode change rather than a slow-down. The previous value of 0 silently permitted hovering mid-corridor.
provenance.speed_max_mps: 80 m/s = 156 kt, below the 170 kt maximum cruise reported for the Joby S4. Declared separately from cruise_mps: the model previously used cruise as both set speed and hard cap, so a gap could only open, never close.
